title: Perry nuclear upgrades would add enough power for 150,000 homes, energy secretary says
source_used: POWER Magazine (own reporting on the DOE announcement); also WSYX and energytech.com. The Cleveland.com page (pool link) returned HTTP 403.
key_facts: On Monday 5 Oct 2026 the US Energy Department's Office of Energy Dominance Financing announced a conditional commitment of up to $4.2 billion in loans to power producer Vistra; Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced it at the Perry plant in Ohio.

The money would finance uprates (upgrades that raise a reactor's output) at Vistra's Perry and Davis-Besse plants in Ohio and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania, with an option for possible future uprates at Comanche Peak in Texas.

The department says the projects could add 433 megawatts of new nuclear capacity, preserve nearly 4 gigawatts of existing output, and support the plants running 20 years beyond their current licences.
The commitment is conditional: Vistra must meet technical, legal, environmental and financial conditions before the loan is made.
The 433 megawatts of uprate capacity is already contracted to Meta under 20-year power purchase agreements Vistra signed in January, according to POWER.
POWER reports Vistra told the Nuclear Regulatory Commission it plans to file for Perry's uprate in the second half of 2029, with the higher power expected in the second quarter of 2031.
The department says the plan will lower electric bills and prevent outages on the PJM grid, which WSYX and energytech.com say spans 13 states and about 67 million people.
Cleveland.com's headline says Wright put the Perry upgrades at enough power for 150,000 homes; this figure is not in the other outlets read.
quote_evidence: The Department of Energy’s (DOE’s) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) has announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance uprates and modernization at Vistra’s Beaver Valley nuclear plant in Pennsylvania and its Davis-Besse and Perry plants in Ohio.
The projects could add 433 MW of new nuclear capacity and preserve nearly 4 GW of existing baseload output, the DOE said.
However, the deal is conditional, meaning Vistra must first clear legal, technical, and environmental reviews before a single federal dollar is given.
why_it_matters_hint: Official, conditional federal money to get more power from existing nuclear plants that serve a 13-state grid, though the extra output is already sold to Meta and arrives years from now.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (announcement at the Perry plant); continues the loan plan Bloomberg reported on 2 Oct 2026, carried in our 3 Oct edition.
notes: Cleveland.com returned HTTP 403, so the story was read at POWER Magazine, WSYX and energytech.com, which agree on the figures. The 150,000-homes figure comes from Cleveland.com's headline only and is attributed to it. Follows item 40 of our 3 Oct 2026 edition (Bloomberg, about $4 billion, unnamed sources).
